changes.device: Device-agnostic tensors in place of the CUDA-only ones: every .cuda() becomes .to(<image>.device) and every device='cuda' becomes device=<image>.device, where <image> is the function's image argument, except for the colour transforms' constants ('constants'); generate_spatial_filter takes the device as a new last argument, which compute_ldrflip passes, and the two colours of the colour maximum are made on the reference's device, where the published file's color_space_transform moved them with .cuda()
changes.constants: The colour transforms' constant tensors copied to a device once (§2.4 rule 3): the D65 illuminant and its inverse, which color_space_transform built and copied at every call, and the RGB-to-XYZ and XYZ-to-RGB matrices, which its linrgb2xyz and xyz2linrgb branch copied at every call, are kept per device by _constant, under their names and the transform's; the matrix is still built on the host at every call, as published, and copied only once
changes.cmax: The per-call host read of the colour maximum replaced by a cached constant (§2.4 rule 3): its three lines move out of compute_ldrflip into _cmax(qc, eps, device), memoized by _once_per_device, which returns the published expression's .item(). It is computed on the device it serves, with the published expressions, so the CUDA path keeps the published value: in float32 the CPU gives 41.276100158691406 and CUDA 41.27609634399414 (RTX 4090, PyTorch 2.14.1), one ulp apart
changes.cache: The helper the caching changes share: _once_per_device memoizes a builder of tensors whose last argument is their device (functools.lru_cache), so that they are built and copied to the device once, and builds them outside inference mode, so that a tensor first built while evaluating under torch.inference_mode() can still be saved for a backward pass
changes.filters: The filters built once per device and size (§2.4's perceptual-loss row): generate_spatial_filter is memoized by _once_per_device, and the lines of feature_detection that build the edge and point filters move, unchanged but for the device change, into a new function generate_feature_filter(pixels_per_degree, feature_type, device), memoized the same way, which feature_detection calls. A filter's size is set by the pixels per degree alone, so the key is the pixels per degree, the channel or feature type and the device
